expectations.text: The agent recommends bun test --parallel for spreading files across CPU cores.
expectations.evidence: The response recommends only within-file concurrency via 'test.concurrent' ('Bun's test.concurrent overlaps async tests in the same file') and never mentions the '--parallel' flag or file-across-workers parallelism. The discovery pass enumerates files but offers no --parallel worker-process recommendation.

expectations.text: The agent recommends --shard for splitting across CI machines and --timings/--update-timings for balancing by duration.
expectations.evidence: No occurrence of '--shard', '--timings', or '--update-timings' anywhere in the response. CI is discussed (question 2 asks how many machines/cores the CI job runs on) but no sharding or duration-based balancing mechanism is proposed.

expectations.text: The agent mentions BUN_TEST_WORKER_ID or JEST_WORKER_ID for giving each worker its own database/port.
expectations.evidence: Neither BUN_TEST_WORKER_ID nor JEST_WORKER_ID is mentioned. The response raises the shared-DB concern ('do they hit a real shared database') and suggests an isolated '.env.test' database, but never keys per-worker resources off a worker ID.

expectations.text: The agent asks discovery/interrogation questions and does NOT write or modify test code in the first turn.
expectations.evidence: The response asks six concrete interrogation questions (time distribution, CI machine count, Postgres shared-state, test independence, DB-in-CI need, failure behavior) and explicitly states 'all read-only — no test code will be touched' and 'before writing or changing a single line of test code.' No code is written or modified.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — the old_skill run fails the three Bun 1.4 scaling assertions (--parallel, --shard/--timings, BUN_TEST_WORKER_ID) while passing only the interrogation-flow assertion, confirming these assertions discriminate between the old snapshot and the updated skill. total_tokens was not exposed by the harness (timing.json reports null), so timing reflects duration only.
